pre_mortem.failure_story: We sized or held American Airlines as a levered recovery stub near $15.14 per share, leaning on mid-cycle operating cash flow near $4.70 per share and Lawrence/synthesis returns of 27–28% per year while the proof-first component schedule base case was −$9.79 per share and dhando was none. We assumed roughly $29 billion of debt and finance leases against $902 million of cash could be paid down from normalized owner cash rather than forcing dilutive refinancing or covenant stress first. A simultaneous earnings trough, fuel and labor cost spike, and credit-market tightening arrived while FY2025 capital spending ($3.779 billion) already exceeded operating cash flow ($3.099 billion). Operating income fell further below the FY2025 $1.467 billion level, trailing operating cash flow per share breached the contract falsifier below $3.50 for four quarters, and maturing debt could not be rolled without equity dilution. The market re-rated the stub from complexity-discount recovery option to distressed equity; hold-period return landed far below the 15.2% bear Lawrence envelope—a severe capital loss on a name with no moat, no bounded bear, and negative filing-locked component value at entry.
